key_insight: Random train/test splits in perovskite-ML benchmarks can drastically overestimate performance because duplicated recipes leak information, so provenance-grouped evaluation is needed to measure true generalisation.
engineering_relevance: For device optimization, this protocol helps researchers choose models and claims that transfer to genuinely new perovskite chemistries, fabrication routes, and institutions rather than to familiar historical records.
method: Mapped institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database.
Built a hierarchy of grouped splits to isolate duplicates, publications, and institutions.
Benchmarked 13 models across increasingly strict evaluation settings.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that nearly two-thirds of curated devices share their exact recipe with another, and that model rankings shift sharply when moving from random splits to unseen institutions and future-discovery splits.
watch_item: Grouped evaluation is more realistic but may reduce apparent scores and requires careful provenance tracking, especially when metadata are incomplete or inconsistently recorded.
paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
